questions.question:
Choose the correct option to give a one-word substitution for the sentence given.
A person who can talk non-stop or can speak continuously.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Garrulous .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Garrulous** refers to a person who talks a lot, often excessively or in a verbose manner.
 
• The other options provided do not match the meaning of the sentence:
 
 
• **Precipitous:** Refers to something steep or sudden, not related to speech.
 
• **Circumvent:** Means to avoid or bypass, not related to talking.
 
• **Sparkling:** Refers to something bright or shining, unrelated to speech.
 
 
• Hence, option 1 (**Garrulous**) is the correct one-word substitution for a person who talks non-stop or continuously.

Correct sentence: *A person who can talk non-stop is **Garrulous**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One-word substitutions are used to express lengthy sentences or phrases in a concise manner.
 
• Examples of similar one-word substitutions:
 
 
• **Loquacious:** Another word for someone who talks a lot.
 
• **Taciturn:** The opposite of garrulous; refers to someone who speaks very little.
 
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.

Neha approached her new hobby with enthusiasm, eager to grasp the basics as a beginner.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Apprentice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes Neha as a beginner who is eager to learn the basics of her new hobby.
 
• The word **Apprentice** refers to a person who is learning a skill or trade under someone more experienced, making it the most suitable one-word substitute.
 
• Other options, such as **Veteran** (experienced person), **Mentor** (guide/teacher), and **Expert** (highly skilled person), do not match the description of a beginner.

Correct sentence: *Neha approached her new hobby with enthusiasm, eager to grasp the basics as an **Apprentice**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Veteran:** Refers to someone with extensive experience in a particular field.
 
• **Mentor:** Refers to someone who guides or teaches others.
 
• **Expert:** Refers to someone with advanced skills or knowledge in a specific area.
 
• **Apprentice:** Refers to someone learning as a beginner, often under the guidance of a mentor or teacher.

questions.question:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.

If you had spoken to my mother, she would tell you where I was.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. tell you .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a **third conditional sentence**, which is used to describe hypothetical situations in the past.
 
• The structure of the third conditional is **"If + past perfect, would have + past participle"**.
 
• In the result clause of the conditional sentence, the verb should be in the form **"would have + past participle"**.
 
• However, the verb **"tell"** in the result clause is incorrect and should be replaced with **"would have told"**.

Correct sentence: *If you had spoken to my mother, she **would have told** you where I was*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1st Conditional Sentence:**

 
 
• **Structure:** If + Present Simple, will + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.
 
• **Usage: **Describes real or possible situations in the future with likely outcomes.
 
 
 
• **2nd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Simple, would + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If I were rich, I would travel the world.
 
• **Usage: **Describes hypothetical or unlikely situations in the present or future.
 
 
 
• **3rd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure: **If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.
 
• **Example: **If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
 
• **Usage: **Refers to unreal past situations and their imagined outcomes.

questions.question:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

I don't understand why the puppy keeps running __over that tree__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. around that tree.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "running over" is incorrect in the context of the given sentence because it implies physically stepping on or passing over the tree, which is illogical.
 
• The correct preposition to use in this context is "around," as it conveys the idea of the puppy running in a circular or surrounding motion near the tree.
 
• Each option was evaluated:
 
 
• **Option 1:** "on that tree" suggests the puppy is physically on top of the tree, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Option 2:** "across that tree" implies moving from one side of the tree to another, which is incorrect here.
 
• **Option 3:** "around that tree" is the most appropriate as it matches the intended meaning of movement near or encircling the tree.
 
• **Option 4:** "No substitution" is incorrect as the original phrase needs correction.
 
 

Correct sentence: *I don't understand why the puppy keeps running around that tree*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Use of Prepositions:**

 
 
• **"On":** Indicates physical contact with a surface. Example: The book is on the table.
 
• **"Across":** Refers to movement from one side to the other. Example: He swam across the river.
 
• **"Around":** Suggests movement in a circular or surrounding manner. Example: They walked around the park.
 
 
 
• Choosing the correct preposition depends on the context and the action being described.

questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

Cut the blue wire all at once; otherwise, you have to throw the entire thing out of the house with your maximum strength.

options.text: Let the blue wire be cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to throw out of the house with your maximum strength.
Let the blue wire cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to be thrown out of the house by you with your maximum strength.
Let the blue wire be cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to be thrown out of the house by you with your maximum strength.
Let the blue wire be cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to be thrown out with your maximum strength of the house by you.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Let the blue wire be cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to be thrown out of the house by you with your maximum strength.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the imperative form, and the passive voice of an imperative sentence typically begins with "Let."
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject.
 
• The correct structure for the passive voice in this sentence is: **Let + object + be + past participle**.
 
• The second part of the sentence, "you have to throw the entire thing out of the house with your maximum strength," is converted to passive voice as "the entire thing has to be thrown out of the house by you with your maximum strength."

Correct sentence: *Let the blue wire be cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to be thrown out of the house by you with your maximum strength*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Passive Voice Structures:**

 
 
• **Imperative Active Voice:** Cut the wire. → **Passive Voice:** Let the wire be cut.
 
• **Present Simple Active Voice:** She throws the ball. → **Passive Voice:** The ball is thrown by her.
 
• **Future Simple Active Voice:** He will complete the project. → **Passive Voice:** The project will be completed by him.
 
 
 
• **Note:** Always ensure the correct placement of "by" and the subject when converting sentences to passive voice.

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
Rajan said to Rini, "I have very often informed you that we have to attend the meeting every Saturday."

options.text: Rajan told Rini that he had very often informed her that they had to attend the meeting every Saturday.
Rajan told Rini that she must very often informed her that they had to attend the meeting every Saturday.
Rajan told Rini that he had very often been informing her that they had to attend the meeting every Saturday.
Rajan told Rini that he had very often informed her that they had been attending the meeting every Saturday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Rajan told Rini that he had very often informed her that they had to attend the meeting every Saturday.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in direct speech and needs to be converted to indirect speech.
 
• When converting direct speech into indirect speech:
 
 
• The verb tense changes based on the reporting verb (past tense here).
 
• Pronouns are adjusted according to the context of the sentence.
 
• Words indicating time or frequency, such as "very often" and "every Saturday," remain unchanged as they do not affect the tense.
 
 
 
• The direct speech, "I have very often informed you that we have to attend the meeting every Saturday," becomes "Rajan told Rini that he had very often informed her that they had to attend the meeting every Saturday." This is because:
 
 
• "Have informed" changes to "had informed" (past perfect tense).
 
• "You" changes to "her" (adjusted for the listener).
 
• "We" changes to "they" (adjusted for the speaker and listener).
 
 

Correct sentence: *Rajan told Rini that he had very often informed her that they had to attend the meeting every Saturday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for changing direct to indirect speech:**
 
 
• If the reporting verb is in the past tense, the verb in the reported clause must be changed to a corresponding past form.
 
• Personal pronouns must be adjusted to reflect the speaker and listener.
 
• Time expressions such as "today," "tomorrow," "yesterday" may need to be changed based on the context.
 
 
 
• **Examples of tense changes in indirect speech:**
 
 
• Simple Present → Simple Past
 
• Present Perfect → Past Perfect
 
• Simple Past → Past Perfect

questions.question:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully.

My cousin lives ____ carter road ____ the bank.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. on, next to.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes a location where the cousin lives in relation to Carter Road and a bank.
 
• The correct preposition for describing a residence on a street is **"on"**. For proximity to another landmark, **"next to"** is appropriate.
 
• Options such as **"at"** are incorrect because "at" is typically used for specific points or locations rather than streets.
 
• Similarly, "besides" and "beside" are less commonly used in this context compared to "next to" for indicating proximity.

Correct sentence: *My cousin lives **on** Carter Road **next to** the bank.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Prepositions:**

 
 
• **On:** Used to indicate a position on a surface or street (e.g., "on Carter Road").
 
• **Next to:** Indicates a position immediately adjacent to something (e.g., "next to the bank").
 
• **At:** Refers to a specific point or location (e.g., "at the corner").
 
• **Beside/Besides:** Beside means "next to" but is less common in modern usage for locations, while besides means "in addition to" and is unrelated to physical positioning.

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

Dinner is being prepared by my sister.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. My sister is preparing dinner .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive voice**, as indicated by the use of "is being prepared."
 
• To change a sentence from passive to active voice, the subject performing the action must be placed at the beginning of the sentence.
 
• The subject in this case is "my sister," and the action being performed is "preparing dinner."
 
• The correct active voice structure is: **Subject + is/am/are + verb + object**.

Correct sentence: *My sister is preparing dinner*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Passive Voice Structure:** Object + is/am/are + being + past participle + by + subject.

 
 
• Example: The book is being read by John.
 
 
 
• **Active Voice Structure:** Subject + is/am/are + verb + object.
 
 
• Example: John is reading the book.
 
 
 
• Option 1: "Dinner prepared my sister" is grammatically incorrect because "prepared" is in the past tense and the structure does not properly indicate the action.
 
• Option 3: "My sister prepares dinner" is in the present simple tense, which does not correspond to the continuous action implied by "is being prepared."
 
• Option 4: "My sister was preparing dinner" is in the past continuous tense, which also does not match the present continuous tense of the original sentence.

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

He asked me if I had ever been to the Louvre.

options.text: He said, "You have ever been to the Louvre?"
He asked, "Do you ever go to the Louvre?"
He asked me, "Have you been to the Louvre?"
He said to me, "Have you ever been to the Louvre?"

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. "He said to me, 'Have you ever been to the Louvre?'".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of **indirect speech**, where a question is being reported.
 
• To convert indirect speech into direct speech for a question, the sentence must:
 
 
• Include quotation marks.
 
• Use the exact question format and wording.
 
• Retain the original tense of the question.
 
 
 
• In direct speech, the question is typically introduced with a reporting verb like "said to" or "asked."

Correct sentence: *He said to me, "Have you ever been to the Louvre?"*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for converting indirect speech to direct speech:**

 
 
• Remove introductory words like "He asked me" or "He said."
 
• Use quotation marks to enclose the exact words spoken.
 
• Ensure proper punctuation, such as a question mark for questions.
 
• Preserve the tense from the original direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Indirect: She asked if I was coming tomorrow. → Direct: She asked, "Are you coming tomorrow?"
 
• Indirect: He wondered whether it was raining. → Direct: He said, "Is it raining?"

questions.question:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
She refrained ____ commenting publicly and instead focused ____ internal communication.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. from, on .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition **"from"** is commonly used with the verb "refrain" to indicate abstention or avoidance of an action. Hence, "refrained from" is grammatically correct.
 
• The preposition **"on"** is used with the verb "focused" to specify the target or area of concentration. Therefore, "focused on" is the correct usage.
 
• Options 2, 3, and 4 use incorrect prepositions, making the sentence grammatically and contextually incorrect.

Correct sentence: *She refrained **from** commenting publicly and instead focused **on** internal communication*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Prepositions:**
 
 
• **From:** Indicates the source or point of abstention (e.g., refrained from eating).
 
• **On:** Specifies the focus or target area (e.g., focused on the task).
 
 
 
• Incorrect Options:
 
 
• **Option 2 (of, in):** "Refrained of" and "focused in" are grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 3 (for, by):** These prepositions do not align with the verbs "refrained" and "focused."
 
• **Option 4 (with, to):** "Refrained with" and "focused to" are incorrect usages.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

She said to him, "You were sleeping."

options.text: She told him that he was sleeping.
She told him that he had been sleeping.
She told him that you had been sleeping.
She told him that she had been sleeping.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. She told him that he had been sleeping .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in direct speech: **She said to him, "You were sleeping."**
 
• When converting a sentence from direct to indirect speech, the pronouns and tenses must be adjusted to match the context.
 
• Here, the past continuous tense in direct speech (**"You were sleeping"**) changes to past perfect continuous tense (**"he had been sleeping"**) in indirect speech.
 
• The pronoun **"you"** is changed to **"he"** to match the subject (**him**) in the indirect speech.

Correct sentence: *She told him that he had been sleeping*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for changing direct to indirect speech:**

 
 
• Change in pronouns: Adjust the pronoun to match the context of the sentence.
 
• Change in tense: The verb tense in the reported speech changes depending on the reporting verb (e.g., past continuous becomes past perfect continuous).
 
• Remove quotation marks: Replace them with conjunctions like **"that"**.
 
 
 
• **Example for practice:**
 
 
• Direct: He said, "I am watching a movie."
 
• Indirect: He said that he was watching a movie.

questions.question: Which sentence from the passage is written in the present perfect tense?

options.text: Every hospital employee plays a critical role.
Many remain committed to their work.
Awareness about the importance of every hospital worker has grown.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the **Present Perfect Tense**, we look for the specific verb structure: **Has/Have + Past Participle (V3)**.
 
• In **Option 4**, the sentence "Awareness... **has grown**" follows this exact formula (*has* + the third form of the verb *grow*). This tense is used to describe an action that happened at an unspecified time in the past or began in the past and continues to the present.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** "Hospitals **operate**..." is in the **Simple Present Tense** (V1).
 
• **Option 2:** "...employee **plays**..." is in the **Simple Present Tense** (V1 + s).
 
• **Option 3:** "Many **remain**..." is in the **Simple Present Tense** (V1).
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In competitive exams, identifying tenses is a foundational skill. Always remember that the Present Perfect ("has grown") links the past to the present, whereas the Simple Past ("grew") would imply the action is finished and disconnected from now.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect:** Subject + has/have + V3 (e.g., has worked, have seen).
 
• **Simple Present:** Subject + V1 (s/es) (e.g., works, see).
 
• **Tireless:** Having or showing great effort or energy.
 
• **Psychological weight:** The mental or emotional burden of a situation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the sentence with a **Modal Verb**, we look for auxiliary (helping) verbs that express necessity, possibility, permission, or ability. Common modal verbs include *can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will,* and *would*.
 
• In **Option 1**, the word **"may"** is a modal verb used to express **possibility** or a likely scenario. The phrase "may have to" combines this possibility with an obligation.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "Emergency ward staff often **faces**..." uses a main verb in the simple present tense. "Often" is an adverb, not a modal verb.
 
• **Option 3:** "...employee **is marked**..." uses a helping verb "is" (part of the passive voice structure), but it is a primary auxiliary, not a modal.
 
• **Option 4:** "Hospital employees **witness**..." uses a simple action verb (V1) without any auxiliary.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level competitive exams, modal verbs are frequently tested because they change the "mood" or "tone" of a sentence. "Nurses attend" (a fact) is very different from "Nurses **may** have to attend" (a potential requirement).*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Modal Verb:** A verb that is used with another verb to express ideas such as possibility, permission, or intention.
 
• **Precision:** The quality, condition, or fact of being exact and accurate.
 
• **Compassion:** Sympathetic pity and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others.
 
• **Around the clock:** Happening all day and all night.

questions.question: What is the main message of the passage?

options.text: Doctors are the only essential workers in a hospital
Hospital employees enjoy easy working hours
Hospital employees need recognition and support
Working in a hospital is fun and relaxing

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the **main message**, we look for the core argument or conclusion the author reaches after presenting all the facts.
 
• The passage describes the **hardships** (long hours, stress, emotional burden) and the **critical roles** played by all hospital staff, not just doctors.
 
• The final paragraph provides the "call to action" or the ultimate point: *"However, **proper recognition, mental health support, and fair working conditions are still essential** to ensure the well-being of those who care for others."*
 
• **Option 3** directly summarizes this need for acknowledgement and better support systems for these workers.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** This **contradicts** the text, which emphasizes that "every hospital employee plays a critical role" and that others' contributions often go "unnoticed."
 
• **Option 2:** This is the **opposite** of the truth; the text states their lives are marked by "long hours" and "entire shifts without rest."
 
• **Option 4:** The passage uses words like "high stress," "emotional strain," and "suffering," which are the opposite of **"fun and relaxing."**
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In competitive exams, the "Main Message" is usually found in the **concluding sentences** of the passage. While the middle paragraphs provide evidence of the struggle, the end explains why that struggle matters and what needs to change.*

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. He created mockups of each screen the user would view in order to build the user interface.

Q. He programmed the app's features and response, writing the fundamental logic.

R. He fixed errors and made sure the app ran well by testing it on a variety of devices.

S. He made the finished product available for download by uploading it to the app store.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. P, Q, R, S .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence parts describe a sequential process of developing and deploying an app.
 
• The correct order must follow the logical and chronological progression of steps in app development.
 
• **P:** This is the first step where the interface is designed by creating mockups of each screen.
 
• **Q:** After the design, the app's core features and logic are programmed.
 
• **R:** Once the app is built, testing is done to ensure it runs well on various devices.
 
• **S:** Finally, the app is uploaded to the app store for users to download.

Correct sequence: ***P, Q, R, S***.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• This type of question tests your ability to understand the logical flow and order of events in a process.
 
• Pay attention to keywords and phrases indicating sequence or steps, such as "created," "programmed," "tested," and "uploaded."
 
• Practicing such questions improves comprehension and sequencing skills.

• Sentence P introduces the subject of the paragraph: a robot built as the students' final assignment.

questions.question: What is the antonym of "Misanthropic"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Sociable .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Misanthropic** refers to the dislike or distrust of humanity or people in general.
 
• The antonym of "Misanthropic" would be a word that reflects a positive attitude towards people or society.
 
• **Sociable** means enjoying the company of others, which is the opposite of being misanthropic.
 
• Other options:
 
 
• **Reclusive:** Refers to someone who prefers isolation, similar to misanthropic.
 
• **Cynical:** Suggests distrust or skepticism, which aligns with misanthropic attitudes.
 
• **Pessimistic:** Indicates a negative outlook, but is not directly related to disliking people.
 
 

Correct sentence: *The antonym of "Misanthropic" is **Sociable**, which represents a positive attitude toward people and society.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Synonyms of Misanthropic:** Antisocial, distrustful, hermit-like.
 
• **Sociable:** Represents friendliness, openness, and willingness to interact with others.
 
• **Context:** Understanding antonyms often involves identifying the opposite traits or qualities described by the word.
</ul
